$comment: The corpus for measuring suggestion.DefaultDuplicateFloor (#532). Author-written and labelled before any similarity was computed; the labels are the groups and the roles, and the pair classes are derived from them by the harness in test/evidence. Titles and notes are content and may be in any language the product indexes; every field name, role and group name is English (rule 13).

roles.anchor: the reference piece of work in its group
roles.duplicate: the same work, paraphrased, in the anchor's language
roles.duplicate-xl: the same work in the other language
roles.near-identical: the anchor with one word or a punctuation mark changed - a control that must sit at the very top of the duplicate band, or the model is the finding
roles.related: the same subject, different work - the hard band the floor has to sit above; `twin` names the item it is a translation of, which makes that one pair a cross-lingual duplicate
roles.namesake: shares a proper noun with the anchor and nothing else - a control that must sit in the unrelated band
roles.single: a group of one; every pair it is in is unrelated

items.title: Preserve both sides of a sync conflict
items.notes: When two devices edit the same field offline, the loser's value must be kept somewhere the person can see it, not silently discarded. The conflict record needs the field, both values, both timestamps and which device wrote each. The UI work is separate; this is the record and the merge rule only.

items.title: Keep the losing value when two offline edits collide
items.notes: Same field edited on two devices while offline: don't throw the loser away. Store a conflict row with the field, the two values, the two timestamps and the two device ids. Rendering it is a separate task - this one is the row and the merge rule.

items.title: Render sync conflicts in the entry's history
items.notes: Show the conflict rows from the sync record in the history view, with the value that lost and a way to restore it. Depends on the record existing first.

items.title: Use a fractional index for offline reordering
items.notes: Two devices reordering the same list offline must not produce a collision on merge; a fractional key between neighbours does that without renumbering.
